newsitem.title: USA: Ohio bill would index income tax for inflation.
newsitem.headline: Ohio bill would index income tax for inflation.

text.p: Ohio lawmakers unveiled a bill Monday that would index the state's personal income tax for inflation.

The bill, which is expected to be introduced in the Ohio General Assembly this week, calls for tax brackets, credits and exemptions in the personal income tax code to be indexed for inflation, according to a press release from the two Republican sponsors in the Ohio House.

The lawmakers said that increases in inflation push taxpayers into higher tax brackets, triggering automatic tax increases for the state without any legislative vote. Inflation also makes tax exemptions and credits worth less, they said.

"Higher tax brackets and lower credits and exemptions are a 'double whammy' on Ohio taxpayers," said State Rep. Bill Schuck, R-Columbus, adding that indexation would "end an unfair hidden tax and put more money back in the pockets of Ohio's working families."

Ohio Treasurer J. Kenneth Blackwell, who hosted a Columbus press conference on the bill, said indexing tax rates to inflation would ensure that taxpayers' incomes are not exaggerated in tax calculations.
Without such a move, he said that inflation would push people into higher tax brackets without an increase in real income income.
"The result is a real increase in taxes, and a family left wondering where the money went," Blackwell said.
Of the 42 states that tax personal income, 17 use indexing, according to materials from the lawmakers.
